035:1: Why do the sons born in the local universe work closer to us than the Paradise Sons?
035:4: In Paper 34 we saw how the local universe Mother Spirit becomes the equal partner of the Creator Son. Now Paper 35 introduces the first children these two brought forth together—the Sons of God of local universe origin.
035:5: The Sons we met earlier were of Paradise origin. In Nebadon there is one Creator Son, Michael; 1,062 Avonals; and an estimated fifteen to twenty thousand Trinity Teacher Sons (35:0.1). Just as the triune Deity of Paradise creates three orders of Sons, the dual Deity of the local universe, the Son and the Spirit, also creates three high orders of sons: the Melchizedeks, the Vorondadeks, and the Lanonandeks. After them come the Life Carriers, who are taken up in the next paper (35:0.2-0.7).
035:6: What work, then, does each of these local universe sons take up, and why has one order never betrayed its trust while hundreds of another have fallen into rebellion?
035:8: ⟦Q 35:2.2⟧They are the hope of every universe group which aspires to self-government; they are the pattern and the teachers of self-government to all the spheres of Nebadon.⟦/Q⟧ (35:2.2)
035:17: The dual Deity of the local universe (Son and Spirit)
035:19: The dual Deity with the next level of the Sevenfold God
035:22: From a new creative union of the Creator Son and the Creative Spirit was born the original Melchizedek, the Father Melchizedek, who co-operated with the two of them in bringing into being the whole group of that name (35:1.1). In Nebadon he is the first executive associate of the Bright and Morning Star (35:1.2).
035:35: The two are never absent from Salvington at the same time
035:37: The Melchizedeks of Nebadon were all created within a thousand years, and because one of their own number functioned as co-ordinate creator, they are an autonomous order partly self-originating. They elect their administrative head every seven years (35:1.3).
035:39: The Melchizedeks are the first order to come so close to the lower creatures that they can minister directly to the evolutionary races without incarnation. They stand about halfway between the highest divinity and the lowest creature life, so they are natural mediators between the two. To every intelligent being they are understanding friends, sympathetic teachers, and wise counselors (35:2.1).
035:40: They show the highest type of true self-government, and not once in all of Orvonton have they betrayed their trust (35:2.2). As the first-born, they patrol the universe on their own and make independent reports to the Creator Son, and as mobile advisory courts they adjust the difficulties of the worlds (35:2.3-2.4). Twelve Melchizedeks accompany the bestowal of an Avonal Son (35:2.6).
035:41: The Melchizedeks are almost perfect in wisdom, but they are not infallible in judgment. When one working alone makes a minor mistake, he receives instruction from the Creator Son on Salvington and returns to service on the third day (35:2.8). Their number does not increase, and more than ten million are on record in Nebadon (35:2.9).
035:43: The Salvington circuit of seventy primary spheres and four hundred and twenty tributaries—four hundred and ninety worlds in all—is the Melchizedek University, and ascending mortals are trained on all these worlds before they attain Salvington residential status (35:3.1). The 490 spheres are divided into ten groups, and the first group is supervised by the Melchizedeks (35:3.2).

035:50: Physical-life schools and laboratories of living energies
035:62: Every mortal who completes constellation training lands on the Melchizedek world, and even after reaching Paradise he will not forget his first day there (35:3.11). On the six tributary satellites of the pilot world, the ascenders review in turn the road of ascent they have traveled (35:3.13-3.19).

035:71: The sojourn on the local system capital
035:73: Experiences on the seventy tributary worlds of the constellation

035:77: The correlation and co-ordination of the five epochs
035:79: The college of high ethics on the Melchizedek home world is presided over by the Father Melchizedek. Nebadon is rather low in spiritual development, but because it has had so many administrative problems it has become a great clinic for the neighboring universes. So more than one hundred thousand outside students are always studying here (35:3.22).
035:81: The Melchizedeks, together with the Trinity Teacher Sons, direct the whole morontia education of ascending mortals (35:4.1). On Edentia they are also known as emergency Sons, and they are the first to hurry to every exigency, whether physical, intellectual, or spiritual (35:4.2, 4.4). They may become temporary custodians of a defaulting planet, and seven times in Nebadon they have served in the likeness of mortal flesh (35:4.4).
035:83: ⟦Q 35:4.2⟧Whenever and wherever special help is needed, there you will find one or more of the Melchizedek Sons.⟦/Q⟧ (35:4.2)
035:85: Melchizedek, the Prince of Salem on Urantia in the time of Abraham, is one such case. With the approval of the planetary trustees, who feared that the light of life might go out in the spiritual darkness, he volunteered to incarnate, fostered the truth of his day, and passed it on safely to Abraham (35:4.5).
035:87: The Vorondadeks, the second order, are better known as the Constellation Fathers, since they head the constellation governments. There are one million of them in Nebadon, and there is no way to increase their number (35:5.1-5.2).
035:92: Less versatile, but more dependable as rulers
035:94: Not their administrative equals, but the greatest stability of purpose
035:96: Errors of technique have occurred, but never rebellion
035:98: They serve as ambassadors to other universes and as consuls representing the constellations, and they are most often entrusted with the full powers of sovereignty (35:5.5). Isolated worlds usually have a Vorondadek observer who can exercise absolute authority in an emergency (35:5.6). Through all this service they have become the historians of the local universe (35:5.7).
035:100: At least three Vorondadeks are assigned to each constellation and serve for 10,000 standard years, about 50,000 years of Urantia time (35:6.1). The one hundred Constellation Fathers form the supreme advisory cabinet of the Creator Son (35:6.2).
035:102: Three Most Highs of a constellation
035:105: The reigning Most High, head of the government
035:107: Oversees spiritual affairs, acts in the Father’s absence
035:109: The physical welfare of the constellation
035:111: At each change of administration the senior becomes head and the junior becomes senior, so a Most High serves on a constellation for about 150,000 Urantia years (35:6.1). No major policy is put into effect unless all three Most Highs agree (35:6.3), and our constellation, Norlatiadek, is at present administered by twelve Vorondadeks (35:6.5).
035:113: On the seven Vorondadek worlds and their satellites, the second group of the Salvington circuit, forty-nine realms in all, ascending mortals receive the culmination of their education in universe legislation (35:7.1). On the constellations they only observed the legislative assemblies; here they take part in the actual enactment of general laws that co-ordinate the pronouncements of the hundred constellations. This instruction is not surpassed even on Uversa (35:7.2).
035:114: New activities await us on these worlds that cannot be described in mortal words. The narrator confesses that revealing them is not forbidden, but there are no words to convey their meaning and no human work to compare them with (35:7.3).
035:116: The Lanonandeks, the third order, are best known as System Sovereigns and Planetary Princes (35:8.1). Being of a lower level of divinity, they became the first students of the Melchizedek University; Nebadon began with exactly twelve million Lanonandeks, who were divided into three classes at the final examinations (35:8.2-8.3). Once classified, they cannot move to another class, and their number is fixed (35:8.7).
035:123: System Sovereigns, assistants on the supreme councils, counselors
035:147: Because the Lanonandeks come closer to the lower creatures, they render greater service, but they also run a greater risk of going astray. Even so, the primary order in particular are the ablest administrators next to Gabriel’s associates (35:8.15).
035:149: System Sovereigns rule in commissions of two or three, and the Constellation Father designates the head every ten thousand years (35:9.2). They are almost sovereign in local affairs and are not supervised by Trinity observers, so this is the one place where disloyalty to the will of Michael can most easily take root (35:9.5).
035:150: In Nebadon more than seven hundred Lanonandeks have rebelled; only three of them were System Sovereigns, and most were Planetary Princes and tertiary Lanonandeks (35:9.6). This is not a flaw in creation; it is because they were given great personal freedom so that they could better understand evolutionary creatures. The higher rulers say that although there are many troubles at first, the higher loyalty of thoroughly tested sons will more than compensate for these trials (35:9.7-9.8).
035:155: A new sovereign installed in a comparatively short time
035:157: Isolated at once; the local spiritual circuits are cut
035:159: Only a bestowal Son re-establishes the lines of communication
035:161: Rehabilitation possible, but never restored to his former post
035:164: On the seven Lanonandek worlds and their forty-two satellites, the third group of the Salvington circuit, former System Sovereigns become teachers of administration. Here the ascenders take part in the actual co-ordination of the administrative pronouncements of ten thousand local systems, and these colleges are surpassed only by the schools of Ensa (35:10.1-10.2). The training sponsored by the Melchizedeks is practical and experiential, a matter of actually doing what has been learned (35:10.3).
035:165: Defaulting Planetary Princes who accept rehabilitation do custodial work here, at least until Nebadon is settled in light and life (35:10.4). Yet many Lanonandeks have made wonderful records of service, and despite the danger of falling into the errors of liberty they are a noble and loyal group (35:10.5).
035:167: Paper 35 shows in turn the three orders of sons brought forth by the Son and the Spirit. The Melchizedeks are the most versatile teachers and emergency ministers, the pattern of self-government who have never betrayed their trust. The Vorondadeks rule the constellations and co-ordinate legislation with unwavering judgment. The Lanonandeks rule systems and planets most closely and so render the greatest service, but having been given great freedom, they also ran the greatest risk of falling. All these sons are also teachers of us ascending mortals, and on the worlds of the Salvington circuit we will learn ethics, legislation, and administration from them and actually practice them. The Creator chose freely tested sons rather than perfect ones, and that choice will in the end bear fruit in a deeper loyalty.

035:178: Wherever help is needed, there is a Melchizedek

035:188: The trials of free-choice sons are repaid by a higher loyalty

036:1: Where does life come from, and how does it take root on a barren planet?
036:4: In Paper 35 we met the Melchizedeks, Vorondadeks, and Lanonandeks, brought forth by the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit. Paper 36 takes up the fourth order announced at the end of that paper—the Life Carriers.
036:5: Life does not arise of itself. Life is constructed according to plans formulated by the Architects of Being, and it appears on the inhabited planets either by direct importation or through the activities of the Life Carriers. The Life Carriers design creature life and carry it to the planets, and after planting life they remain for a long time to foster its development (36:0.1).
036:6: What kind of beings, then, are the Life Carriers? Who gives the spark of life to the material they organize, and how does that life grow into beings with mind and will?
036:8: Concept is inherent in the Father, expression in the Son, and life realization in the Spirit. (36:6.7)
036:12: The Life Carriers are the only group of intelligent life within a local universe in whose creation the rulers of a superuniverse take part. They are the offspring of three: the Creator Son, the Universe Mother Spirit, and one of the Ancients of Days. The only beings who can decree the extinction of intelligent life also take part in creating those who establish life (36:1.1).
036:13: One hundred million Life Carriers were created in Nebadon. They are directed by the life-determining trio of Gabriel, the Father Melchizedek, and Nambia, the first-born Life Carrier (36:1.2). The Melchizedeks tested them and divided them into three divisions, and they accompany them every time they go out to plant life on a new planet (36:1.3).
036:18: Subdivided into twelve groups of specialists by form of life manifestation
036:20: Study and help with the protection and conservation of life
036:22: Specialize in handling and guarding the life patterns
036:25: The seven primary worlds of the fourth group of the Salvington circuit are the worlds of the Life Carriers, and each has six satellites (36:2.1-2.9). The headquarters world has a college of life planning to which teachers come even from Paradise, and the central focus of the seven adjutant mind-spirits is also located there (36:2.10).
036:30: Study of universal life in all its known phases
036:32: Designing new modes of life organization
036:34: Developing ways to protect and conserve life
036:36: The evolution of creature life and its antecedents

036:38: The phases of mind interrelated with life

036:42: Unrevealed domains related to the Supreme Being
036:44: The realms of life are marked not by the decimal system but by three, seven, and twelve and their combinations. The life pattern of Orvonton consists of twelve inheritance carriers, and the human sex cells of Urantia contain forty-eight units of trait control (36:2.11).
036:45: The outline of the life design is given by the Creator Son and its execution is left to the Life Carriers; plans that depart from established formulas must be approved by the Creator Son (36:2.12). Urantia is a decimal planet, one in ten worlds, a life-experiment world, so greater variation from the standard designs was permitted (36:2.15). Even life forms that seem useless are all needed for the full functioning of higher intelligent life (36:2.17).
036:47: Life does not appear spontaneously; the Life Carriers must initiate it on barren planets (36:3.1). The commissioned corps usually consists of one hundred seniors, one hundred assistants, and one thousand custodians, and Urantia’s life was organized on the spot after their arrival, according to approved formulas (36:3.2).
036:49: ⟦Q 36:3.4⟧The vital spark—the mystery of life—is bestowed through the Life Carriers, not by them.⟦/Q⟧ (36:3.4)
036:51: The Life Carriers formulate the life plasm and stir matter as living catalysts, but the spark that enlivens the body and presages the mind comes from the Universe Mother Spirit. They transmit nothing of their own personal nature (36:3.4-3.5).
036:54: What the Life Carriers may do
036:55: Implantation period (about half a million years)
036:56: May plant life and add new forms
036:58: Manipulate the environment and steer evolution favorably
036:60: Their work ends — they may not interfere with will
036:62: They leave; some volunteer to stay as counselors
036:64: On Urantia too, two senior Life Carriers and twelve custodians took vows of temporary renunciation, stayed as counselors, and are still serving (36:3.9).
036:66: Every local system in Nebadon has one midsonite world on which Melchizedeks functioned as Life Carriers. There a materially modified Melchizedek Son mated with a daughter of the material order, and their offspring are called midsoniters (36:4.1-4.2).
036:70: Until the standard age of one thousand
036:71: Live as reproducing beings on their home world
036:73: Translated by seraphic transport; they lose the privilege of reproduction
036:75: None has experienced death; all are alive
036:77: The seventh world of the finaliters on Salvington
036:79: They are not indwelt by Adjusters, so they can hardly be called immortals, yet they do not seem to be mortals either (36:4.4). The fifth group of the Salvington circuit is the worlds of the finaliters, and many areas there are closed even to ascenders (36:4.6-4.7). The finaliters do not speak of the destiny of the midsoniters, and the Melchizedek Life Carriers believe that they will one day receive transcendental spirits from God the Ultimate (36:4.8).
036:81: Evolution on the primitive worlds is not accidental but purposeful because of the presence of the seven adjutant mind-spirits. As children of the Universe Mother Spirit, they make up her personal ministry to material minds (36:5.1). Yet they are not separate personalities; they are more like circuits, practically one level of consciousness of the Divine Minister (36:5.4).
036:86: Quick perception, reflex instincts, sense of direction, self-preservation
036:88: Association of ideas, quick reasoning and judgment
036:90: Fidelity, the root of character and moral stamina
036:92: Curiosity for adventure and discovery, the scientific spirit
036:94: The social urge, species co-operation, the gregarious instinct
036:96: The religious impulse, the first distinction marking ensouled beings
036:98: The tendency of progress that co-ordinates all the adjutants
036:101: ⟦Q 36:5.11⟧Worship is the badge of spiritual-ascension candidacy.⟦/Q⟧ (36:5.11)
036:103: The adjutants grow experientially but never become persons, and because the first five function in animals, animals are essential even to the intellectual evolution of man (36:5.13). Mind is cared for by different ministers at different stages (36:5.15).
036:107: Before it can learn from experience
036:110: The exclusive domain of the adjutant spirits
036:112: Supermind, the spirit circuit of the Mother Spirit
036:114: Even personal mind has no survival qualities unless it identifies with spirit. Mind that functions without spiritual insight, without the capacity to worship and to long for survival, is not immortal (36:5.17).
036:116: Life is both mechanistic and vitalistic, and it is not inherent in matter. The scientists of Urantia will understand protoplasm more deeply, but they will never make a living organism (36:6.1). Life comes only from life, mind from pre-existent mind, and spirit only from spirit ancestors (36:6.2).
036:122: The initial spark of life, the breath of life
036:123: The Spirit of God (the Universe Mother Spirit)
036:125: The Mother Spirit, through the adjutant spirits
036:127: Personally imparted by the Mother Spirit
036:129: At death plant and animal life remains only as cosmic force, without identity or personality; it does not survive individually. The survival of mortal creatures depends wholly on the evolution of an immortal soul within the mortal mind (36:6.5). The source of the life-activating spark is not fully understood even by the narrators; they know for certain only that life flows from the Father through the Son and by the Spirit (36:6.7).
036:131: Paper 36 shows that life is not a product of chance but a gift that is designed, carried, and guarded. The Life Carriers organize the patterns and tend the environment, but the spark of life, mind, and the power of reproduction come from the Mother Spirit. The seven adjutant mind-spirits guide evolution with purpose, from intuition to wisdom, and when the spirit of worship awakens, the creature becomes a candidate for spiritual ascension. And the moment beings with will appear, the Life Carriers take their hands off. From then on our future depends on our choices and on the immortal soul growing within our minds.
036:136: Propagators of life, created with the participation even of a superuniverse ruler
036:138: On seven worlds life is designed, conserved, and studied
036:140: Life is given through them, and their work ends when will appears
036:142: The midsoniters do not die; they are gathering for the future
036:144: From intuition to wisdom; worship is the badge of ascension candidacy
036:146: Life comes only from life; the spark comes from the Spirit
036:149: Life is conceived in the Father, expressed in the Son, and realized in the Spirit, and our survival depends on the soul that grows within our minds.
037:1: What personalities stay beside us as we ascend, tending this universe as one great school?
037:4: In Papers 35 and 36 we met the created orders of sonship of the local universe. Paper 37 follows on from them. It deals chiefly with the universe aids, an intermediate group standing between the ministering spirits and the ascending sons, and it also takes a brief look at the higher spirits stationed in Nebadon and the permanent citizens of the local universe (37:0.2).
037:5: At the head of all these personalities stands the Creator Son, Michael, and with him the Divine Minister of Salvington, his equal in divinity and his complement in creative attributes. These two Creators are, in a very literal sense, the Father-Son and the Spirit-Mother of all the native creatures of Nebadon (37:0.1).
037:6: Who, then, are the many personalities who work under them? How do they help and teach us, the pilgrims of time, and who are those who stay beside us forever?
037:8: ⟦Q 37:6.2⟧The entire universe is one vast school.⟦/Q⟧ (37:6.2)
037:16: One in each universe, the first-born chief executive
037:20: High spirits who help creature survival and ascension
037:30: The Bright and Morning Star is the first-born of the native creatures of a local universe; in Nebadon he is Gabriel of Salvington. He is the personal representative of the Sovereign Son and the spokesman of his creative consort (37:1.9). In the early days he worked almost alone, but as the universe grew, unrevealed assistants and the corps of Evening Stars were added (37:1.10).
037:32: The Evening Stars are superangels planned by the Melchizedeks and brought into being by the Creator Son and the Creative Spirit; they serve chiefly as Gabriel’s liaison officers (37:2.1). Gabriel cannot be in two places at once, so at the conclaves of Salvington, often a thousand of them held at the same time, the Evening Stars represent him (37:2.2). When sent on special missions to planets, they have sometimes been known as the angel of the Lord (37:2.3).
037:43: This corps is never closed to ascenders until the universe is settled in light and life (37:2.4). In ascendant assignments a created Evening Star and an ascendant Evening Star always work as a pair (37:2.7). They are the personalities of highest rank who accompany the missions of the Avonal bestowal Sons, and they administer the sixth group of the Salvington circuit (37:2.8, 2.10).
037:45: The archangels are offspring of the Creator Son and the Universe Mother Spirit, the highest spirit beings produced in large numbers in a local universe; there are nearly eight hundred thousand in Nebadon (37:3.1). They are one of the few groups outside Gabriel’s jurisdiction, and they are devoted not to routine administration but to helping mortals survive and ascend (37:3.2).
037:46: Remarkably, a divisional headquarters of the archangels has recently been established on Urantia. Visitors from outside soon take a great interest in this little planet when they learn it is Michael’s bestowal world (37:3.3). This foreshadows the future gathering of other ascendant activities here and adds solemn weight to the Master’s promise (37:3.4).
037:48: This undoubtedly presages the future concentration of other ascendant activities on the bestowal world of Michael and lends a tremendous and solemn import to the Master’s personal promise, “⟦Q 37:3.4⟧I will come again⟦/Q⟧.” (37:3.4)
037:50: One hundred archangels accompany every Paradise bestowal Son, and two seniors become the personal aids of an Avonal. The one who proclaims the closing roll call of a dispensation is the archangel of the resurrection, Michael’s archangel (37:3.5-3.6). On the archangels’ worlds, the seventh group of the Salvington circuit, are the personality recorders, who preserve the personality records between death and resurrection (37:3.7-3.8).
037:52: The Most High Assistants are volunteers who originate outside the local universe and are temporarily attached as representatives or observers of the central universe and the superuniverses; they always number far more than millions (37:4.1). Perfectors of Wisdom, Divine Counselors, Solitary Messengers, supernaphim, and others help Nebadon come into greater harmony with the ideals of Paradise (37:4.2).
037:53: They work under the supervision of the Trinity ambassador, and when they serve on request, they voluntarily place themselves under the jurisdiction of the leader of that realm (37:4.3). They serve in local universe and constellation capacities and are especially useful in upholding plans that call for more mature foresight (37:4.4-4.5).
037:55: The High Commissioners are ascending mortals who have attained immortality by fusing not with an Adjuster but with a spirit fragment of the Mother Spirit. On some worlds the Adjuster indwells only temporarily and leaves forever when life ends (37:5.1-5.2). They usually stop at Salvington and serve the local universe forever; they do not become finaliters but are registered in the local universe corps of perfection (37:5.2-5.3).
037:62: A spirit fragment of the Mother Spirit
037:64: Paradise, the Corps of the Finality
037:65: Usually Salvington, the local universe corps of perfection
037:68: Deep experiential wisdom about the problems of Nebadon
037:70: They begin as racial commissioners on the planets, representing the viewpoints of the races and striving to win mercy and justice for them; there are a little over one and a half billion in Nebadon (37:5.5-5.6). They sit as advisers in all the courts, speaking for those who cannot speak for themselves (37:5.7, 5.9). The eighth group of the Salvington circuit is their permanent residence (37:5.10-5.11).
037:72: The education of Nebadon is jointly administered by the Trinity Teacher Sons and the Melchizedeks, but much of the work of maintaining and developing it is done by more than three million celestial overseers. They are volunteers qualified by experience who travel the universe inspecting the techniques of the schools (37:6.1). From the human worlds to the mansion worlds, the seventy realms of Edentia, and the 490 spheres of Salvington, the entire universe is one vast school (37:6.2).
037:74: This is the keynote of the whole educational system: character acquired by enlightened experience. (37:6.3)
037:76: The method of education is first to assign a task and then to teach the divine way of doing it best; work and teaching are closely linked (37:6.4). Mind and spirit grow together, and we come to enjoy a unified mind that no longer has to referee contests between spirit and flesh (37:6.6). Most Urantia mortals will have the opportunity to serve for a time in this corps before leaving Nebadon (37:6.7).
037:78: The Mansion World Teachers are recruited and glorified cherubim, commissioned by the Melchizedeks like the other teachers. They carry most of the education of the morontia career, and their number is beyond the grasp of the mortal mind (37:7.1). More about them follows in later papers (37:7.2).
037:80: Besides the power centers and physical controllers, high spirit beings of the family of the Infinite Spirit are permanently assigned to the local universe (37:8.1). Among them, Andovontia, the tertiary universe circuit supervisor, carried out the isolation of Urantia at the time of Caligastia’s betrayal, and he sends greetings, gladly looking forward to our return to the universe circuits one day (37:8.3).

037:87: Supervises the spirit and morontia circuits; carried out Urantia’s isolation
037:89: Census Director, cognizant of the birth and death of will
037:91: Representative of the Supreme Executive of Orvonton
037:93: Traveling courts, about one hundred million commissions
037:95: About half a billion, living law libraries
037:97: Seventy-five seniors, almost four billion students
037:99: Seventy billion, ministering on the transition planets
037:101: Each universe has its own native corps of angels, but it also receives help from higher spirits from outside. The present chief of seraphim on Urantia is a primary supernaphim of Paradise (37:8.10).
037:103: The local universe too has orders of permanent citizens who, by and large, neither ascend nor descend. Their growing experience continues to serve the universe at the level of their origin (37:9.1-9.6).
037:110: Offspring of Son and Spirit; close to the Spirit-fused mortals
037:116: A reproducing order; some become planetary Adams
037:119: Custodians who keep the continuity of planetary administration
037:121: The Material Sons are the Creator Son’s personalization of his final concept of being in the dual form of male and female; they are the origin of the original Adam and Eve of each system (37:9.9). Mortals stay only a short while on a planet and then leave, and celestial ministers come and go, but the midway creatures remain until the age of light and life as the planet’s actual custodians and citizens (37:9.11).
037:123: Nebadon will grow from its present more than three million inhabited worlds to ten million, and countless beings work on its 647,591 architectural spheres (37:10.1). The spironga, spirit offspring of the Morning Star and the Father Melchizedek, help with routine spirit work, and the spornagia, beings of an animal order, take care of the material upkeep of the headquarters worlds (37:10.2-10.3).
037:124: When ascending mortals reach Salvington, they too are assigned to almost every celestial corps as helpers, students, observers, and teachers. At each level of attainment they reach back a hand to the fellows who follow them (37:10.5). This paper is only a brief outline of the personalities who tend the universe as a great training school, and the pilgrims of time will be lovingly sent on from world to world until at last they reach Paradise and the destiny of finaliters (37:10.6).

038:1: Who are the angels who work beside us, and how is the gap between the material world and the world of spirit bridged?
038:4: In Paper 37 we surveyed the many personalities of the local universe. Now Paper 38 turns to the group among them who come closest to mortals—the ministering spirits of the local universe. The personalities of the Infinite Spirit fall into three orders—angels, authorities, and powers—and the angels are the ministering spirits of time (38:0.1).
038:5: Just as the central universe has its supernaphim and the superuniverses their seconaphim, in the local universe the seraphim, together with the cherubim and sanobim, make up the angelic hosts (38:0.2). The seraphim are very uniform in design; of all the spirit types of personal beings they are the closest to a standard (38:0.3).
038:6: How, then, are these angels born and trained, and what kind of relationship do they have with us? And who bridges the great distance between humans bound to matter and pure spirit, and how?
038:8: ⟦Q 38:2.4⟧Angels do not sit in judgment on mankind, neither should individual mortals prejudge their fellow creatures.⟦/Q⟧ (38:2.4)
038:12: Seraphim are created by the Universe Mother Spirit. Since the creation of the pattern angels in the early days of Nebadon, seraphim have been projected in unit formations of 41,472 at a time (38:1.1). While the Creator Son was occupied with creating the Material Sons, the Universe Mother Spirit for the first time engaged in solitary spirit reproduction, and this was the beginning of the creation of the seraphic hosts (38:1.1).
038:13: This order of angels is projected at the time of planning the evolution of mortal will creatures. The seraphim who worked in Nebadon before that were lent for a while by a neighboring universe (38:1.2). Because Nebadon is still in the making, seraphim are still being created periodically (38:1.3).
038:25: Angels have no material bodies, but they are definite individual beings. We cannot see them, but they perceive us just as we are in the flesh. They share human feelings and emotions, enjoy music, art, and genuine humor, and know well our moral struggles and spiritual difficulties. They love human beings (38:2.1). They are not creatures of sex emotion, but they are deeply affectionate, and on planets with sex they are usually referred to with feminine pronouns (38:2.2).
038:26: In personal status angels are not very far from humans, but in certain functions they far surpass us. They know things like the number of hairs on your head without the effort of counting; they are truly mathematical prodigies (38:2.3). Yet they are not our judges or accusers; they are to be loved, not worshiped (38:2.4-2.5). When we lay aside the flesh, we become very much like them (38:2.6).
038:28: ⟦Q 38:2.5⟧You do well to love them, but you should not adore them; angels are not objects of worship.⟦/Q⟧ (38:2.5)

038:44: Besides these there are six orders of unrevealed angels. They are never called seraphim or ministering spirits, and they are wholly occupied with the administrative and other work of Nebadon, apart from the spiritual ascent of man (38:3.1).
038:46: The ninth group of the Salvington circuit—seven primary spheres, each with six tributary satellites, forty-nine worlds in all—are the seraphic worlds. Here every seraphim has a real home, and that home is the residence of two seraphim; they live as pairs (38:4.2).
038:47: Seraphim exist not as male and female but as negative and positive, and most assignments require two angels. This union is due mainly to function, not to sex emotion (38:4.3). They gather for reunions every thousand years, and seraphim who cannot leave their posts attend alternately with their complements (38:4.4).
038:49: Seraphic training is a long process that begins on Salvington and passes through the constellation and the system to commissioning. The first seraphim of Nebadon were trained by a corps of one thousand seraphim from Avalon, and since then senior angels have taught their juniors. The Melchizedeks also play a large part in the education of all local universe angels (38:5.1).

038:124: The midway creatures are classified as ascending Sons of God, but in their ministry to mortal men they are reckoned with the ministering spirits of time (38:9.1). 039:1: How do seraphim, born of the same mother, divide into seven branches of service, and where do they at last arrive?
039:4: In Paper 38 we looked at the origin and nature, the training and organization of the seraphim. Now Paper 39 spreads out the concrete picture of the angelic hosts—where these seraphim actually work and what they do. The Universe Mother Spirit seeks to produce uniformly perfect seraphim, but for reasons unknown her offspring are very diverse, and after training they invariably fall into seven groups (39:0.1).
039:5: This does not mean that any seraphim are inferior to another group. Every angel is at first limited in service to the group of its birth, but through experience and education angels can acquire skill in other services. Manotia, the supreme seraphim who co-operated on this paper, has achieved all seven services (39:0.9-0.10). Remarkably, the angels of higher ability most persistently seek the lower services, especially that of planetary helpers (39:0.11).
039:6: Where, then, does each of these seven hosts work and what does it do, and how is all that service interwoven with our ascent?

Because they have no direct connection with Urantia at present, a detailed account is omitted (39:7.2).

Angels are not sure of their eternal future until they reach Seraphington, but no angel who has reached it has ever gone astray (39:8.9).
039:155: For angels who have attained the Father of spirits, the career of time is over. The higher an angel’s ability, the more it wants to come down to a lower place, and the summit of its service is the path of the guardian angel who walks with a mortal. And at the end of that path the completed angels come back to us and remain forever our true friends. The one thing all their service teaches us is to choose sincerely, wherever we are, to do the will of God.

040:1: How does a lowly mortal of animal origin become a son of God, and do different destinies mean different measures of love?
040:4: In Papers 38 and 39 we met the angels and midway creatures who serve beside us. Now Paper 40 turns to those who receive that service—the ascending Sons of God who climb toward Paradise. This narrative began with the Deities and has come down the scale of being until at last it reaches the lowest life with the potential of immortality. The narrator himself is a Mighty Messenger who was once a mortal of an evolutionary world (40:0.10).
040:5: Seven classes of ascending sons have been revealed (40:0.1-0.8). From the lowly mortal of animal origin to the Personalized Adjuster, their story is a glorious record of divine love and gracious condescension reaching across all the universes (40:0.9).
040:6: On what grounds, then, are mortals like us called sons of God, and how do the destinies of those who fuse with the Adjuster differ from those who do not? And does that difference mean there is a difference in the Father’s love?
040:8: ⟦Q 40:10.13⟧Sonship is the supreme relationship of the creature to the Creator.⟦/Q⟧ (40:10.13)

Guardian seraphim too, through their experience and service with ascending mortals, attain the status of ascending sonship; they reach Paradise by way of Seraphington, and many enter the Mortal Corps of the Finality (40:1.1). For an angel to climb to the summit of finaliter attainment is a far greater achievement than our survival with the help of an Adjuster (40:1.2).
040:32: The Material Sons are by origin descending sons, the Adams and Eves who come down from the system capital to the inhabited worlds (40:2.1). When they have fully accomplished their mission as biologic uplifters and that world is settled in light and life, they may withdraw from planetary duty and register as perfected Material Sons. They are then recognized as ascending sons and begin the long journey toward Havona and Paradise together with mortals (40:2.2).
040:34: The Paradise ascent of the midway creatures is long delayed, but when their planet reaches the middle ages of light and life, they are released from planetary service. They are registered as ascending sons and set out for Paradise by exactly the same route as the mortal races (40:3.1).
040:41: All the Mortal Corps of the Finality
040:44: A mortal’s failure to survive is never due to neglect on the part of the Adjuster. The Adjuster left behind returns to Divinington and may be sent again to the worlds of time. After such repeated service, or after serving as the indwelling Adjuster of a bestowal Son, competent Adjusters are personalized by the Universal Father (40:4.1).
040:45: Originally prepersonal beings, they became experiential beings by sharing in the lives of lowly mortals. The personality they receive comes from the Father’s experiential bestowal of personality, so the Personalized Adjusters are the highest order of the ascending sons (40:4.2).
040:47: Mortals are the last link in the line of those called the sons of God. The reach of the Eternal Son comes down through personalizations ever less divine and more human until it reaches beings we can see and touch, while the reach of the Infinite Spirit finds its limit in the angels (40:5.1-5.2). The Father cannot come down in that way, but because he is within us as the Adjuster, the One who is farthest from us in personality and spirit is in fact the nearest (40:5.3).
040:48: Spirit identification is the secret of personal survival, and mortals are divided into three series according to their relationship with the Adjuster (40:5.4). We can hardly yet be called ascending sons, but through faith and free-will co-operation with the Adjuster we can attain that status. When we fuse forever with the Adjuster and the two become one, we become in fact ascending sons of God (40:7.2).
040:82: Because the Father has given us himself, he asks of us, “⟦Q 40:7.4⟧Be you perfect, even as I am perfect⟦/Q⟧” (40:7.4). Adjuster fusion is the divine guarantee of Paradise attainment, and these are the only order of humans who pass through Havona and find God on Paradise (40:7.5).

040:87: Spirit fusion takes place not during life but only upon reawakening on the mansion worlds. Fusion never overlaps; a creature fuses with only one—Father, Son, or Spirit (40:9.1). 040:88: The difference is memory. Human memory survives by means of the transcript held by the Adjuster, but Spirit-fused mortals lack that mechanism, so they awaken like newly created beings.
